title: No-Bake Cannabis Cookies: Oatmeal, Cherry and Pecan
h1: No-Bake Cannabis Oatmeal Cookies with Tart Cherries and Pecans
metaDescription: Stovetop no-bake cannabis oatmeal cookies with cherries and pecans: cannabutter added off the heat, exactly 12 even cookies, gluten-free and vegan swaps.
excerpt: Chewy chocolate-oat cookies made on the stovetop, with cannabutter stirred in after the boil and the batch shaped into exactly 12 so the math stays simple.
keyTakeaways: Boil the sugar, evaporated milk, cocoa and plain butter for 1 minute; the cannabutter goes in off the heat.
Shape exactly 12 cookies, so each one carries a twelfth of the THC.
Store them in a labeled, airtight container in the fridge, apart from everyday snacks.
Certified gluten-free oats, plant-based butter and coconut milk make easy swaps.
body:
These no-bake cannabis cookies are chewy chocolate-oat rounds with tart cherries and toasted pecans, made on the stovetop with no oven. Stirring the cannabutter in after the one-minute boil spares it the hottest step, and shaping exactly 12 cookies keeps the math simple.

## How to Dose No-Bake Cannabis Cookies

The boil uses plain butter only. Off the burner, stir in the measured cannabutter, fold in the oats and shape 12 equal cookies, each holding a twelfth of the THC. To estimate your butter's strength, start with our [cannabutter guide](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/).

They're for adults 21 and older. Eat one, then wait a full 2 hours before reaching for a second ([dosing basics](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/)).

## Ingredients

Quick oats set more firmly than old-fashioned ones, and evaporated milk makes a richer base than regular milk. Pecans, tart cherries, cocoa, vanilla and salt carry the flavor; peanut butter is optional. Making fresh cannabutter? Order flower ahead from your nearest [High Society store](/shop/) for in-store or curbside pickup.

## Three Moments That Matter

1. **The boil.** Start the minute once bubbles cover the surface. Too short and the cookies stay soft; too long and they crumble.
2. **Off the heat.** Mix the cannabutter in completely before the oats go in.
3. **Portioning.** Weigh the mixture and divide by 12, or use a level scoop.

## Storage and Labeling

Store the cookies airtight in the fridge, labeled "THC" with the date and the dose per cookie, and keep them out of sight: to a child, they look like any other cookie. Keep Poison Help's number, 1-800-222-1222, handy, and call a veterinarian if a pet eats one.

## Gluten-Free and Vegan Swaps

Certified gluten-free oats, with every add-in checked for gluten, make a gluten-free batch. For vegan cookies, use plant-based butter in the boil, full-fat coconut milk instead of evaporated milk, and an infusion made with coconut oil or vegan butter. Prefer an oven? Try our [cannabis cookie recipe](/blog/cannabis-cookie-recipe/).

faq.q: Why add the cannabutter off the heat?
faq.a: To keep each cookie's dose predictable. Off the burner, you have time to blend the butter evenly before the oats go in, and the infusion skips the boil, which runs hotter than plain boiling water. Long or very high heat can cost THC, so there's no reason to boil it.

About a week, sealed airtight and refrigerated, which also keeps them firm. For longer storage, freeze them in a single layer, then bag and label them and thaw one at a time. Either way, the dose per cookie belongs on the label.

Not automatically. Oats contain no gluten themselves, but cross-contact with wheat, barley or rye is common, so regular oats can carry some. If gluten matters to you or someone you're sharing with, buy oats labeled certified gluten-free and check the add-ins. If you have celiac disease, ask your doctor or a dietitian first: research suggests most people with it can eat moderate amounts of oats, but not everyone.

ingredients: 1¼ cups quick oats (certified gluten-free if needed)
⅓ cup pecans, toasted and chopped
⅓ cup dried tart cherries, chopped
2 tablespoons plain unsalted butter, for the boil
2 tablespoons butter for after the boil: your measured cannabutter, topped up with plain butter (see the dosing note)
steps: Line a tray with parchment. Combine the oats, pecans, cherries and salt in a bowl.
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, stir together the sugar, evaporated milk, plain butter and cocoa. Bring to a full rolling boil and boil for exactly 1 minute, stirring.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the cannabutter blend, the peanut butter if using, and the vanilla until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Fold in the oat mixture until every oat is coated.
Portion 12 equal mounds onto the parchment with a level scoop, or weigh the mixture and divide by 12.
Chill for about 30 minutes, until set, then store in a labeled airtight container in the fridge.
recipe.dosingNote: **THC per cookie = THC in the cannabutter you add ÷ 12.** Estimate your butter first: grams of flower × THC percentage (as a decimal) × 1,000 gives the most THC it can hold. For example, 3.5 g of flower labeled 16% THC, infused into 1 cup (16 tablespoons) of butter, comes to at most 560 mg, roughly 35 mg per tablespoon. One tablespoon of that here, with 1 tablespoon of plain butter, means no more than about 3 mg per cookie. Decarboxylation and infusion lose some THC, so these figures are ceilings, not promises. Start low with one cookie, give it 2 hours, and keep the labeled container somewhere kids and pets can't reach.

sources.label: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions
Wang M. et al. (2016), Decarboxylation study of acidic cannabinoids, Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research
National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIH): Eating, diet and nutrition for celiac disease (oats and cross-contact)

review.summary: 15 claims checked: 13 ok, 2 fixed (0 wrong, 0 unsupported, 2 overstated); 3 ok claims also got precision or wording edits.

claims.claim: The cookies are for adults 21 and older
Eat one, then wait a full 2 hours before reaching for a second (body, dosing note)
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch 2026-10-24): "it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug"

claims.claim: Adding the cannabutter after the one-minute boil protects the dose (intro); FAQ: "To protect the THC"
claims.fix: softened: intro now "spares it the hottest step"; the FAQ now leads with even, measured mixing and says the infusion skips the boil, adding "Long or very high heat can cost THC, so there's no reason to boil it". Measured losses need long heating or far higher heat than a one-minute boil (the site's own cannabutter recipe decarbs at 240°F for 30 to 45 minutes), so the off-heat step is a precaution
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang et al. 2016, full text via Europe PMC): its own extracts, heated at 80-145°C for up to 60 min, showed THCA plus THC "decreased slightly"; the "significant loss" it cites (Veress et al.) came "at longer times" at 145°C

claims.claim: A rolling sugar boil runs hotter than plain boiling water (FAQ)
claims.source: https://www.ipm.org/amomentofscience/boiling-point-candy.php (Indiana Public Media / Indiana University, WebFetch 2026-10-24): "At sea level, pure water boils at two hundred and twelve degrees and never gets any hotter"; "As the water boils out, the solution gets more concentrated and the boiling point goes up."

claims.claim: High heat can break THC down (FAQ; now "Long or very high heat can cost THC")
claims.fix: wording: tied to long or very high heat, so the one-minute sugar boil is not presented as a THC threat
claims.source: Wang et al. 2016 full text: describing Dussy et al., "At 300°C, a significant loss of Δ9-THC was observed"; describing Veress et al., "a significant loss at longer times" at 145°C

claims.claim: Boil timing: too short and the cookies stay soft, too long and they crumble; quick oats set more firmly than old-fashioned oats; evaporated milk makes a richer base than regular milk
claims.source: general cooking knowledge (evaporated milk is milk with much of its water removed); no health claim

claims.claim: Each of 12 equal cookies holds a twelfth of the THC (takeaway, body)
claims.fix: none (holds when the cannabutter is mixed in completely and the mixture is weighed or scooped level, as the article says)

Dose math: flower grams × THC fraction × 1,000 is the ceiling; 3.5 g at 16% THC in 1 cup of butter is at most 560 mg, about 35 mg per tablespoon; 1 tablespoon here is no more than about 3 mg per cookie; decarboxylation and infusion losses make these ceilings
claims.fix: wording: "Eat one cookie" became "Start low with one cookie" so the note says to start low and wait (arithmetic checked: 3.5 × 0.16 × 1,000 = 560; 560 ÷ 16 = 35; 35 ÷ 12 = 2.9)
claims.source: arithmetic; Wang et al. 2016 (decarboxylation converts THCA to THC with some loss); build contract section 4 recipe rule

review.notes: Independent fact-check: the CDC FAQ and the NIDDK page were reopened with WebFetch; Wang et al. 2016 was read through Europe PMC; the sugar boiling-point line was checked against Indiana Public Media's A Moment of Science (Indiana University). High Society facts used: order ahead for in-store or curbside pickup, with flower as a menu category; no product said to be stocked, and no phone, hours, address, payment, prices, deals or app. The two overlap reviews ("in a medium saucepan over medium heat", "butter and cocoa bring to a") are stock cooking phrases under the 8-word limit and were left as written. Writer's notes: GENERALIZE: no branded infused chocolate; homemade cannabutter only. Dose figures are labeled ceilings from a worked example. Texture notes (quick oats, boil timing) and the one-week fridge life are general cooking knowledge, not cited.
